articles.title: Store User Documents: Database Blobs vs Object Storage for Large Files — 5 Decision Rules
articles.excerpt: Short answer: for most SaaS document uploads, put the bytes in object storage and keep searchable metadata in Postgres or MySQL. That split is usually cheaper to scale and gives the application a smal…
articles.body: Short answer: for most SaaS document uploads, put the bytes in object storage and keep searchable metadata in Postgres or MySQL. That split is usually cheaper to scale and gives the application a smaller, faster database; it also keeps the audit trail explicit instead of hiding a file inside a row. The scenario here is a media service processing receipts and retaining the original upload for audit. Large-file throughput is the deciding constraint. A receipt may be small today, but a scanned contract or a high-resolution invoice can turn a comfortable database design into a backup and replication problem. Start with the audit record, not the bucket Treat the database row as the source of truth for document state.

articles.title: When Delay JS Breaks a WordPress Mobile Menu (and PageSpeed Looks Fine)
articles.excerpt: My WordPress website was scoring in the high 90s on mobile PageSpeed Insights. The layout looked right, the navigation worked on desktop, and the mobile view in browser DevTools behaved as expected. T…
articles.body: My WordPress website was scoring in the high 90s on mobile PageSpeed Insights. The layout looked right, the navigation worked on desktop, and the mobile view in browser DevTools behaved as expected. Then I picked up my phone and tapped the hamburger menu. Nothing happened. I tapped again. Sometimes the menu opened, sometimes it didn't. On a site where navigation is one of the first things people use, this is not a small detail. It also made the PageSpeed result feel rather less impressive. This is a short account of what I tested, what changed, and what I still couldn't confirm. It wasn't a controlled performance experiment, and I don't want to turn one incident into a universal rule about WordPress caching.

articles.title: Sloth Nap: two lines in the morning, instead of the chores you keep skipping
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 3: Slow and Steady Sloth Nap is for the evening you do not want to deal with the pile. You drop a chore table and a couple of n…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 3: Slow and Steady What I Built Sloth Nap is for the evening you do not want to deal with the pile. You drop a chore table and a couple of notes into a folder. It ranks which tasks you are likely to skip again, finds the one sentence in the notes that actually has a date, looks up the question you were avoiding, and leaves two lines for the morning. On the sample pile, those lines are the receipts and a one-sentence reply to the landlord. Together they are about 55 minutes. The plants, the dentist, and the downloads folder can wait. Nothing is deleted. Copying the notes into an archive folder stays pending until a person approves it, and a second approval does not copy them again.

Treat a binary BMFont v3 block size as the payload length after the block header. Advance past the one-byte type and four-byte size, then consume exactly that payload. articles.title: Patch Your PHP: What PHP2Shell Means for WordPress Sites
articles.excerpt: PHP released 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35 on October 21 to fix two critical vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, nicknamed PHP2Shell. Both are rated 9.2 out of 10 (CVSS v4.0) an…
articles.body: PHP released 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35 on October 21 to fix two critical vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, nicknamed PHP2Shell. Both are rated 9.2 out of 10 (CVSS v4.0) and let an attacker run code on your server without logging in. The bugs are in PHP itself, the runtime underneath WordPress, so updating WordPress or your plugins won't fix them. I have WordPress sites on SiteGround, and when this news hit, my only question was whether I was vulnerable. I hadn't heard anything from SiteGround, and working out which PHP version my sites actually run took longer than I wanted it to. This is the quick writeup I was looking for, for developers who know their stack and just want the answer without spending an afternoon on it. Am I Affected?

articles.title: Who Actually Buys a Mobile App, and Who Never Will
articles.excerpt: Two sales calls, same script, same price. The first one is over in under a minute: the owner is polite, says it sounds interesting, and never replies again. The second one ends with the owner asking h…
articles.body: Two sales calls, same script, same price. The first one is over in under a minute: the owner is polite, says it sounds interesting, and never replies again. The second one ends with the owner asking how soon it can be in the App Store. Nothing about the pitch changed. What changed was who was on the other end of the phone. Learning to tell those two apart before you dial is most of this job, and it has very little to do with what industry they are in. You are not selling an app. You are selling the second visit. An icon on someone's home screen is a standing invitation to come back. That is the entire product. Everything else — the design, the push notifications, the native screens — exists to make the second visit easier than it was before.

articles.title: The 2027 total solar eclipse will plunge these 10 ancient Egyptian temples and monuments into darkness
articles.excerpt: The "eclipse of the century" will plunge some of ancient Egypt's most spectacular sites into darkness on Aug. 2, 2027. These temples, tombs and monuments are inside the path of totality.
articles.body: The total solar eclipse on Aug. 2, 2027, has an ancient feel. It will certainly be a celestial event for the ages — at 6 minutes 23 seconds, it will feature the longest totality on land of the 21st century and the longest anywhere until 2114. However, its point of greatest eclipse occurs just a few miles from Thebes, the magnificent religious and political capital of ancient Egypt's Middle Kingdom and New Kingdom. On the east bank of the mighty Nile is Luxor, the great city of the living, with its massive temple complexes of Karnak and Luxor. On its west bank is the city of the dead, which includes the Valley of the Kings and the Temple of Hatshepsut. Modern Luxor, population 285,000, is set to become a focal point for eclipse chasers on Aug.

articles.title: Van Gogh's 'The Starry Night' depicts the sky on July 22, 1889, researchers find
articles.excerpt: Researchers think they might have pinpointed the exact night sky that we see depicted in Vincent van Gogh's iconic painting "The Starry Night."
articles.body: Researchers think they might have pinpointed the exact night sky that we see depicted in Vincent van Gogh's iconic painting "The Starry Night." Perhaps one of the most famous paintings in modern history, Van Gogh's "The Starry Night" carries a legacy that continues to inspire and mystify generation after generation. But while you might see in its swirls of color and bright spots of starlight a night sky derived purely from imagination, some scientists think it represents an actual view — one that includes a waning crescent moon, Venus and the Hyades cluster. And they may know exactly when this sky appeared.. In a new study, researchers suggest that "The Starry Night" depicts the pre-dawn sky seen around July 22, 1889 from Saint-Rémy-de-Provence, where Van Gogh painted it.
